items.stem: Where are per-record transaction outcomes stored?
items.explanation: Each record's outcome is recorded in StarBridge's EntityTransaction table; the console shows summary counts.

misconceptions.a: The console shows counts, but the per-record outcomes persist in EntityTransaction — that's what you query when triaging.

items.stem: Run 1 creates a Staff record. On run 2 the source data for that staff is byte-for-byte identical. What outcome does run 2 produce for that record?
items.explanation: A mapping exists and nothing changed since last run, so the engine takes no action: NoChangesDetected.

misconceptions.a: NewEntityCreated only happens when there's no mapping and it's not a duplicate; here a mapping already exists.

options.text: Yes — it means processing failed and must be investigated
No — a preprocessor deferred the record (e.g. a dependency isn't in the destination yet); it will be retried
Yes — it is the same as ExceptionThrown
No — it means the record was successfully created

items.explanation: Rejected means the record can't be processed *right now* (often a missing dependency) and another attempt should be made later. It is explicitly not an error.

misconceptions.c: ExceptionThrown is the error outcome; Rejected is a deferral.
misconceptions.a: Treating Rejected as a failure leads to chasing non-problems.

items.stem: A source record has no existing mapping, and the engine determines it is genuinely not already in the destination. What outcome results?
items.explanation: No mapping + not a duplicate → a new destination record is created: NewEntityCreated.

misconceptions.b: That outcome applies when dedup finds the record DOES already exist in the destination.

items.stem: A daily run that normally reports mostly NoChangesDetected suddenly reports thousands of NewEntityCreated. What is the most likely concern?

options.text: Everything is fine — new records are good
Mappings may have been lost/not found, so existing records are being recreated as new (risking duplicates)
The source feed returned zero records

items.explanation: Records that should match existing mappings are instead being created fresh — a sign mappings aren't being found, which can duplicate the destination. Outcomes are how you spot this.

misconceptions.c: Zero source records would show up as deletions/garbage collection, not a surge of NewEntityCreated.

items.stem: Explain how the transaction outcomes are just delta detection (L1.4) and mapping (L1.6) made visible. Use NoChangesDetected and NewEntityCreated as examples.
rubric: Outcomes reflect the engine's decision tree: is there a mapping? did the delta show a change? is it a duplicate?
NoChangesDetected = mapping exists (L1.6) AND the delta found no change (L1.4)
NewEntityCreated = no mapping exists (L1.6) AND not a duplicate, so a record is created
items.sampleAnswer: Each outcome is the recorded result of the engine's mapping-then-delta logic. NoChangesDetected means a mapping was found (L1.6) and the snapshot matched last run's state (L1.4), so nothing was done. NewEntityCreated means no mapping was found and the record wasn't a duplicate, so a new destination record was made. Reading outcome counts is reading that logic in aggregate.
